name: Carlingford Lough
text: Carlingford Lough is a sea inlet of striking size. It runs ten miles long and two miles wide. The water separates County Down from County Louth. Down lies in Northern Ireland, Louth in the Republic. Dundalk stands nine miles to the southwest. Much of the great Cattle Raid of Cooley unfolds on this water. The Newry Canal links the lough to Lough Neagh. The town of Carlingford sits on the southern shore of Louth. Shallow river crossings mattered to the early Celts before ferries and bridges came. Ritona stood among the Continental Celtic goddesses of river crossings and was honoured at Trier in modern Germany. Clashes at fords appear in old tales. A fight between Cuchulainn and Ferdiad in the Tain Bo Cuailnge stands as the chief of them. Irish and Scottish Gaelic folklore also knows the washer at the ford.
